### South Carolina Industry Leaders Go Behind the Scenes at Dominion Energy, Discuss State’s Energy Future


11/10/2026


[Download this Press Release (opens in new window) PDF 142 KB](https://s205.q4cdn.com/611413639/files/doc_news/2026/11/South-Carolina-Industry-Leaders-Go-Behind-the-Scenes-at-Dominion-Energy-Discuss-State-s-Energy-Future.pdf)


WATCH: Video of the event can be found at[this link.](https://vimeo.com/1244259635/bbe3e59285?share=copy&fl=sv&fe=ci) Please credit Dominion Energy.


**CAYCE, S.C. (Nov. 10, 2026)** South Carolina’s rapid growth and rising energy demand took center stage as business and industry leaders gathered at Dominion Energy’s Cayce headquarters to discuss how to reliably power the state’s energy future.


Approximately 50 business leaders and industry stakeholders got a behind-the-scenes look at Dominion Energy’s operations as they learned more about what is required to reliably serve South Carolina’s energy customers every day.


With energy among its key focus areas, South Carolina Manufacturers and Commerce has an active South Carolina Energy Council. It brings together industry leaders, subject matter experts, and employers to shape energy policy, share insights and advance the Palmetto State’s economic competitiveness.


“South Carolina is one of the fastest growing states in the nation, which means that we've got growing demands on our energy infrastructure,” said Sara Hazzard, SCMC president and CEO. “We wanted to bring together partners from all across South Carolina to talk about the energy needs, issues and opportunities that we have to ensure we’re meeting the needs of a growing state.”


In addition to presentations and a roundtable discussion, attendees and partners also visited Dominion Energy’s system control room, electric dispatch center and customer service facilities.


“Energy touches everybody, not just from a manufacturing and a commercial perspective, but all the way down to individual households,” said Keller Kissam, president of Dominion Energy South Carolina. “This is a great opportunity to allow the council and other state leaders to get a better understanding about the critical nature of our system and what our family of employees do day in and day out to power South Carolina.”


**About Dominion Energy**


Dominion Energy (NYSE:[D](https://investors.dominionenergy.com/home/default.aspx) ), headquartered in Richmond, Va., provides regulated electricity service to[3.6 million](https://www.dominionenergy.com/our-company/operating-segments) homes and businesses in Virginia, North Carolina, and South Carolina, and regulated natural gas service to 500,000 customers in South Carolina. The company is one of the nation’s leading developers and operators of regulated[offshore wind](https://www.dominionenergy.com/projects-and-facilities/wind-power-facilities-and-projects/coastal-virginia-offshore-wind) and[solar](https://www.dominionenergy.com/projects-and-facilities/solar-energy-facilities-and-projects/virginia-solar-projects) power and the[largest producer of carbon-free electricity in New England](https://www.dominionenergy.com/projects-and-facilities/nuclear-facilities/millstone-power-station) . The company’s mission is to provide the[reliable, affordable, and increasingly clean energy](https://www.dominionenergy.com/our-company) that powers its customers every day. Please visit[DominionEnergy.com](http://www.dominionenergy.com/) to learn more.


About South Carolina Manufacturers and Commerce
[www.myscmc.org](http://www.myscmc.org/)


South Carolina Manufacturers and Commerce is the unified voice for businesses across the Palmetto State. This new organization is one of the largest and most powerful advocacy organizations in the history of South Carolina. The merger of the South Carolina Manufacturers Alliance and the South Carolina Chamber of Commerce brings the business community together to speak with one unified voice, bolster its presence in Columbia, expand its reach across South Carolina and align its goals.
